mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% (UNRATE < 5.0%) signals a tight labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are rising (monthly change > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A level of industrial production below 100.0 (INDPRO < 100.0) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during late-cycle regimes defined by unemployment rate below 5.0% and employment above 140,000 thousand persons.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and (UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS > 140000), or negative returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and (UNRATE >= 5.0% or PAYEMS <= 140000).

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 240.0 (CPIAUCSL > 240.0) indicates elevated inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 240.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly employment level above 142,000 thousand persons (PAYEMS > 142000) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 142000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past month signals strong consumer demand for housing, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when HOUST is rising (monthly change > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A level of industrial production below 100.0 (INDPRO < 100.0) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, but only during high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 240.0).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and CPIAUCSL > 240.0.
